library: a curated collection of books or a place where they are kept and organized for reading
folio: a single sheet folded to make two leaves, or a book made from such sheets; also a portfolio of work
editorial: relating to editing or to the distinctive visual language of a publication
typography: the art of arranging type to make language visible, including choice of font and spacing
stylus: a pen-shaped input tool for precise touch, pressure and tilt on a screen
annotation: a note added to a text to explain or highlight a passage
highlight: to mark text with a translucent color so it stands out, like real ink on paper
lasso: a closed-loop gesture that circles an area to select or extract it
extraction: the act of pulling out a selected diagram or text block for reuse
bionic: relating to bionic reading, where the start of each word is bolded to guide the eye
velocity: speed in a given direction; here, reading speed smoothed over time
estimator: an on-device algorithm that predicts time remaining from recent page-turn deltas
progress: how far through a book or chapter the reader has advanced
chapter: a main division of a book, usually with its own title
paragraph: a block of text relating to a single thought, separated by spacing
text: written words that convey meaning on a page
book: a set of written pages bound together, physical or digital
author: the writer or creator of a book
title: the name given to a book or chapter
cover: the outer front surface of a book, often showing title and imagery
image: a visual representation such as a diagram or photograph
diagram: a simple drawing that explains an idea, often needing margin space trimmed
palette: a chosen set of colors, here deep green, burgundy and amber
amber: a warm xanthous yellow (#F7B538) used for highlights and progress
burgundy: a rich dark red (#780116) for active states and tags
green: a deep grounding color (#004F39) for library and dark mode backgrounds
serif: a classic typeface with small strokes at letter ends, suited to long reading
sans: a clean typeface without serifs, used for headers and UI labels
header: a prominent title at the top of a page or chapter
body: the main running text of a book, set in a readable serif
immersive: edge-to-edge presentation that fills the screen for focused reading
edge: the outer boundary of the screen or page
adaptive: automatically adjusting layout for different screen sizes
tablet: a larger touch device that can show a two-page spread in landscape
phone: a small handheld device showing a single immersive column
landscape: horizontal orientation, wider than tall, used for the book spread
column: a vertical block of text; phones use one, tablets use two
spread: two facing pages shown side by side like an open codex
codex: an ancient manuscript book with pages bound together, ancestor of modern books
pressman: a craftsman who operates a printing press with care for margins
margins: the blank borders around a text block that let the page breathe
kerning: micro-spacing between letters that evens out the texture of a paragraph
bookmark: a saved position so the reader can return where they left off
marginalia: notes written in the margins of a book
notebook: a small book for jotting words and ideas to remember
vocabulary: the set of words a reader knows and looks up to expand
ledger: a quiet record of where reading paused and resumed
privacy: keeping reading data on-device without sending it to a server
craft: skillful making where details like typography matter
ribbon: a fabric bookmark, here amber, that holds a place
shelf: a horizontal support where books are stored and displayed
arrival: the act of reaching a place, like the first chapter's opening
morning: the early part of the day when light is soft
light: illumination that falls across pages and screens
warm: gently heated, or describing a welcoming color tone
paper: the material of pages, here warm and paper-coloured
wash: a soft, even spread of light or color
shelves: plural of shelf, the deep-green library storage
promise: an assurance that a spine or title holds something worth reading
air: the surrounding atmosphere, here carrying the scent of ink
ink: pigmented fluid used for printing, simulated here with Multiply ink
cedar: a fragrant wood, evoking the smell of shelves
satchel: a small bag for carrying books
finger: a digit used to scroll or to draw a lasso with touch
row: a horizontal line of books on a shelf
volume: a single book, especially a quarto
quarto: a book made from sheets folded twice, a compact size
cloth: fabric covering a hardcover, here burgundy
catalogue: a list of books available in the library
city: the bustling place outside the quiet library
trams: electric streetcars humming in the distance
lamp: a light source with an amber tick marking reading time
weight: the satisfying heaviness of paper in the hand
marginal: relating to the margins where notes live
extractor: a tool that pulls out a circled diagram or text
dictionary: a local word list that gives definitions without network
definition: the meaning of a word as given by a dictionary
on-device: processing that stays on the phone or tablet for privacy
word: a single unit of language that can be looked up
sentence: a group of words that forms a complete thought
syllable: a unit of sound containing a vowel, used to find the first part of a word
onset: the initial consonants before the first vowel in a word
nucleus: the central vowel or vowel cluster of a syllable
coda: the consonants that close a syllable after the vowel
reading: the act of interpreting written text
speed: how quickly the eye moves across lines, aided by bionic anchors
anchor: a contextual snippet that keeps a highlight attached to its paragraph
context: the surrounding words that help locate a highlight after edits
orphan: a highlight whose anchor text no longer exists and is left detached
publisher: the entity that may push typo fixes to an EPUB file
typo: a small error in text that an update may correct
offset: a position measured in characters or bytes that shifts after edits
lcs: Longest Common Subsequence, a diff that finds shared text between versions
diff: a comparison that shows what changed between two texts
myers: an alternative diff algorithm to LCS for locating anchors
concept: an idea or character extracted by TF-IDF as distinctive
x-ray: a per-book, per-chapter index of characters and terms via TF-IDF
character: a person in a story, often the most distinctive term in a chapter
location: a place in a story that TF-IDF may surface as distinctive
jargon: specialized terms that appear unusually often in one chapter
term: a single word or phrase considered distinctive by frequency
frequency: how often a word appears, used in TF-IDF scoring
inverse: a measure of how rare a term is across the whole book (IDF)
distinctive: standing out because it appears notably more in one chapter
algorithm: a deterministic set of steps, here on-device without AI
deterministic: always producing the same result for the same input, private and fast
network: communication with a remote server, which Folio avoids for privacy
private: kept on the device, not sent elsewhere, as an editorial choice
curated: carefully selected and organized, like the library grid
grid: a tidy arrangement of book covers in rows and columns
thumbnail: a small preview image of a book cover
illustration: a flat, cohesive drawing used for empty states
onboarding: the first experience that welcomes a new reader
import: bringing an EPUB file from device storage into the private library
storage: the app's private files where imported books and covers are kept
picker: the system file dialog (Storage Access Framework) for choosing an EPUB
corrupted: a file that cannot be parsed because its data is damaged
epub: a reflowable ebook format based on ZIP, HTML and OPF metadata
